changes: Every clan's page now says whether sacred sites were recorded. The Clan Stewards were asked for the outer boundary and the sacred sites, so whether a clan recorded any is part of the answer, and "none recorded" is as much a finding as a count. Reported by number and area only; locations are not shared and appear on no map or layer.

Counting them meant reading what the steward wrote. Only three features in the whole dataset are tagged as a sacred site. The usual way one was recorded is the way the rest of the land is recorded — the steward walked around the place and filed the circuit as a land boundary, because to a clan every named parcel inside the outer boundary has a boundary, and the boundary of a sacred site is a boundary. Those arrive as a closed ring inside the outer one, and only the steward's own note says what the ring is. Three clans recorded sacred sites: Juaiko, Rondi and Sukandi.
